Commentary.Commentary: The visitors have put up a decent first innings score courtesy two knocks, one from Elgar and the other from de Kock. Windies will want two of their batters to do something similar, probably go on and get a ton. They need to put up a better show with the bat or they could be staring down another defeat. The visitors will want to repeat what they did with the ball in the first Test. The wicket seems good for batting but there is something in it if you hit the right lines and length. Stay tuned for the second session which could be a good one.
One can say it was a combined effort by the Windies pacers with almost everyone taking a wicket at least. Mayers though has to be the pick with a three-fer but everybody played their part.

It all began with Roach getting Mulder early on in the session. De Kock though continued and along with Maharaj added another handy stand. Both though fell in quick succession with the African skipper falling 4 short of a ton. The last two wickets did frustrate Windies a little but they did not let them go past the 300-run mark.

A really good bowling effort from the hosts this morning and they have done really well to keep South Africa under 300. However, one feels that the visitors do have an edge right now but they will be a little disappointed to not cross that mark.

10 am local (1400 GMT) - GOOD NEWS! The inspection is done and we due for a start at 10.30 pm local (1430 GMT)! Pad up, folks.
We have some sad news to begin with! The start of play on Day 2 has been delayed as there is some rain around. An inspection will be held at 1000 local.

Windies on the other hand, will look for wickets quickly. The second new ball is available and if they can make use of it, they can surely keep the visitors to under 250. An important first session awaits...

A partnership though, a good stand can see the tide completely into their favor. They would be hoping to get over the 300-run mark. De Kock is set and Mulder has started well. A lot will depend on the two if they are to cross that score as there is not a lot of batting to come.

218 for 5 at Stumps on Day 1! South Africa with the edge? Windies ahead or evens-stevens? Quite difficult to say but judging by how the track played and if the first Test is anything to go by, the visitors surely have their noses ahead but by just.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

Now South Africa will hope these two can continue and take them past 300. Windies will want to not let them go above that mark. They do have the option to take the second new ball so one probably assumes they would take it the first thing on Saturday and look to make early inroads. Do join us for all the action. Till then, take care and goodbye!

The Windies bowled decently but they could have used the conditions a lot better. There were way too many harmless deliveries. Yes, there were a lot of them which went past the outside edge but they did lack discipline. Gabriel was probably the pick. Roach, Mayers and Seales took one each. Holder bowled brilliantly but just did not have luck on his side.

Elgar and Kyle got their side to safer shores with a very good stand. Elgar went onto score a half ton but Kyle did not make most of the start he got. De Kock then continued his good form and he along with Elgar added another 50-run stand before Dean fell 23 short of a ton. Those three though have ensured the visitors finish Day 1 slightly ahead.

End of an attritional day of Test cricket. It all started with rain delaying the start of play. Once the showers passed away, it was the Windies who won the toss and elected to bowl. They started off brilliantly by getting three wickets quickly. The first session belonged to them easily but after that, it was all South Africa.

A good session for South Africa! Both Elgar and Kyle played solidly at the start. They took their side to safer shores with a good stand. Elgar got to his half ton but Kyle was dismissed just before the break! The game is quite even at the moment but Windies will have to break the current partnership quickly or de Kock can take the game away from them quickly. An important session awaits.
A single as this is pushed through covers.
Outside off, left alone.
On middle, blocked.
Outside off, left alone.
A short one, it is ducked under.

OUT! THERE IS A SPIKE ON ULTRA EDGE! Not sure why that was reviewed. Maybe Kyle did not realize it. A short one down the leg side. Kyle looks to pull. It goes off the face of the bat. The keeper dives to his left and takes it. Kyle reviews after having a chat with his skipper but replays show that South Africa lose a review. Kyle walks back after getting off to a start. However, he did play the perfect foil to Elgar. Windies finally get the breakthrough. Can they build on this now?
Commentary.Howout: c Joshua Da Silva b Shannon Gabriel

Commentary.Commentary: A huge appeal and the river is raised! Kyle is give out caught behind. He reviews.

NO BALL AND FOUR! That is a streaky way to get your fifty up. A very hard-working innings. He has rode his luck here and there but take nothing away from the resilience he has showed. He expects a short one and he gets it. He looks initially looks to move away but then realizes it keeps coming in. He looks to leave but it goes off the bat and over the keeper for a boundary.

FOUR! In the air... in the gap! Almsot an action reply of how he got out in the first Test but this finds the gap. Full and outside off, Elgar looks to drive with an open face of the bat. It goes wide of the gully fielder and into the point fence. Runs starting to come now.

DRINKS! A good hour for South Africa! They haven't lost a wicket but haven't scored a lot. Scoring though has not been easy but the imoortant thing is, they have probably gone past the tough phase. The ball ain't swinging as it was and the wicket has eased off. Can they now cash in or will Windies find the breakthrough after the break?

It’s been tough going for South Africa. Their batters have struggled. They are on the back foot at the moment but they would know, the longer they stay in the easier it is going to be. Dean Elgar and Kyle Verreynne have done well to hang in there but they need to cash in. Can they do so? We will find out after the break.

A solid session from the Windies. They will be pretty pleased after electing to bowl. Their pacers were excellent. They got the ball to swing and have gotten three wickets in it. Also, they have made it very difficult for the visitors to score. More of the same is what they would want after the break.

Especially against someone who is getting the ball to jag back in nicely. This lands a little wide outside off from the wide of the crease. The angle is already bringing it in, Rassie shoulders arms to this one without covering the off pole and it hits the top of it. South Africa in big trouble now.

DRINKS! A really good hour passage of play for the Windies. They elected to bowl in friendly bowling conditions and have got two wickets inside the 15 overs. Also, they haven't let the visitors score freely too. More of the same is what they would want. South Africa on the other hand, needs to build a stand and they will hope these two can hang in there. Will they fightback?

West Indies PLAYING XI - Kraigg Brathwaite (C), Kieran Powell, Shai Hope, Kyle Mayers, Jermaine Blackwood, Roston Chase, Joshua Da Silva (WK), Jason Holder, Kemar Roach, Jayden Seales, Shannon Gabriel (PLAYING IN PLACE OF Rahkeem Cornwall).

South Africa PLAYING XI - Dean Elgar (C), Aiden Markram, Keegan Petersen, Rassie van der Dussen, Kyle Verreynne, Quinton de Kock (WK), Wiaan Mulder, Keshav Maharaj, Kagiso Rabada, Anrich Nortje, Lungi Ngidi
TOSS- West Indies have won the toss and have opted to field.
Update - 0940 local (1340 GMT) - GOOD NEWS! The rain has stopped and the covers are coming off. Toss in 10 minutes.

Update - 0926 local (1326 GMT) - We should have had the toss by now but guess what? IT IS RAINING! It seems the rain gods have no mercy on men's cricket today. The forecast is also not that promising. Fingers crossed for now.

A clinical performance in the first Test saw the visitors take a 1-0 lead in the series. They just need to avoid a defeat in this game if they are to win the series. Windies on the other hand, need a win, however, judging by the first game, they need to be a lot better than they were if they are to even challenge the away side. Will there be an even contest between bat and ball this time? Toss and teams in a bit...
